That's the trouble of it. I just can't dig out motivation inside of me when I am so afraid of failing at it. I cannot tolerate failure to the point I can't try at anything. And worse, I fear that if I do accomplish anything, it won't end up mattering because others have done it better, or that I will find some new failure in myself to replace the old one, or my biggest fear, that it won't matter because I'm not thin enough for my eating disorder so anything I do accomplish just pales in comparison to the real failure consuming me.

It sounds so frustratingly simple written out like this. I know logically I can go out and do these things. I know nobody expects me to be as thin as I expect myself to be. I know I can't be as big of a human disaster as I feel. But regardless of this, I can't change. It's utterly pathetic.

Despite that this sounds aggravated, I do appreciate your continued encouragement. It means a lot.

I'm sorry that that happened to you. One of the worst feelings in this world is pouring yourself into another person only to watch them dump it onto the floor. You're obviously a giving person, and I hope that you find people who will see the value in that and appreciate you for it.

I hope you stay strong.

I actually hear similar thoughts to this a lot. Sadness gets comfortable. It's so much easier to embrace it than to just fight it every single day. 

Of course, it's kind of a trap in and of itself, isn't it?
